otherProblems: Gym logos are set on large circular plates of their own (dark disc for the white logo, light disc for the dark one), floating between the corner tag and the name rather than integrated with the boxer block (G-4, G-5).

Under long values the hierarchy inverts: the mixed-case gym-and-record line ('Kaunas BC · 14-3', 'St. Michael's ABC · 11-2') is set far larger than the boxer's name, which shrinks to fit (G-4, G-5, G-8 to G-11). The gym name also has no field of its own and is crammed into the record line.

Unbalanced sides under stress values: one corner has a big one-line name and a small record while the other has a small two-line name and an oversized record, so the halves no longer mirror each other across the split (G-8 to G-11).
With empty values the blue half is just a lone 'BLUE CORNER' tag on an empty field (G-6, G-7).
The lock state is only signalled by the WINNER badge turning from yellow to white, a very weak cue for a locked decision (G-52 to G-57).
answer.reasons: With the brief's own values the card is clean: a strong red/blue split, a readable weight-class bar, good diacritics, and a clear winner/loser dimming. Select, lock and clear all work. But the gym logos, which the brief asks for, only appear on large circular plates of their own. With long values the record/gym line becomes the largest text on the card, bigger than the boxer's name, and the two corners stop matching. A director would send it back for the logo treatment and the type hierarchy rather than air it as is.

otherProblems: Each team logo sits on its own bordered square tile. The right-hand crest is on a bright off-white plate that stands out hard against the dark glass bar (G-2, G-4, G-5, G-11, G-14, G-91). The left logo is on a separate dark tile with a yellow outline (G-90). Both read as logos on plates of their own rather than as part of the bar.
Next map pressed from the pre-match state changes nothing visible (G-47 to G-52). The bar stays on KARTTA 1, so no frame shows the map ever advancing.
The live phase word is 'LIVE' in English, while the other three phases use Finnish words (ENNEN OTTELUA, TAUKO, LOPPU).
answer.reasons: The scorebug is clean and centred at the top. Names, map score, series pips, map label and phase pill are all readable on video, light and busy grounds. The long two-line stress names stay inside their fields with no clipping, and the Take and Out animations are tidy. Go live, pause, resume and final all show a visible phase change. What keeps it off air is how the logos are mounted: each one is boxed in its own square tile, and the burgundy crest sits on a bright white plate that pulls the eye away from the bar. A designer would fix the contrast another way instead of giving the logos their own plates. A smaller issue: Next map shows no visible change in any frame.

otherProblems: The panel is a fixed width: with the sample values (G-2) the text ends around x≈1450, leaving roughly 370px of empty dark panel on the right.
A faint short orange line at the bottom right of the panel (around x 1680–1795, y 224) reads more like a stray mark than a deliberate timer bar.
With empty values (G-8 to G-10) the panel shows only 'DONATION' and the placeholder heart, with a lot of empty space.
The white shield avatar fills its orange ring right to the inner edge (G-72), a slightly tight fit.
answer.reasons: A clean, readable donation card at the top right: the dark panel with an orange edge bar holds an orange label, white name and grey message with good contrast on the light, busy and video backgrounds. The long umlaut username fits on one line, the long message wraps cleanly onto two lines, and the white avatar sits clearly inside its orange ring. Hold, resume, replay and skip all behave correctly in the frames, and the Update and Out are clean. The fixed-width panel leaves some empty space on the right with short values and there is a faint stray-looking line at the bottom right, but neither breaks the graphic.

otherProblems: Suspense only dims all four nominees a little (white to grey), so viewers will barely see a change on the cue.
The winner is shown only by a gold-highlighted card with a soft glow. There is no 'WINNER' label, so the moment is understated for an awards night.
Once the winner is revealed, the other three nominees are dimmed to low contrast. That is deliberate and still legible, but it is close to the limit.
When the category is updated, the nominee text shrinks slightly and the layout shifts.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board with a double gold frame, a gold kicker line and a heavy white category title. The four nominees sit in equal cards, two by two, with their text centred and well padded. It reads clearly over the dark, light and busy backgrounds because the panel is opaque. The long category name fits on one line inside the frame. Long director names wrap neatly onto two lines within their cards, with nothing clipped or overlapping. The empty-values frame shows just the centred title, which is fine. Both operator actions the brief needs are on the surface: suspense dims the field and reveal lights up the winning card in gold. The take-in and take-out animations are clean. The only issues are small ones (a subtle suspense state, no explicit winner label), and none of them would stop a director putting this on air.

otherProblems: Each gym logo sits on its own circular plate (a dark disc behind the white logo, a white disc behind the dark logo), so the badges read as stickers rather than part of the card (G-4, G-5, G-65, G-66).

When a gym name is present, it merges into the record line ('Kaunas BC · 14-3', 'St. Michael's ABC · 11-2') and is set larger and heavier than the boxer's name. The secondary data then outranks the fighter (G-4, G-8, G-10).

With long values the two corners no longer match. The red name shrinks to a much smaller single line while the blue name stays large (G-8), or the reverse (G-10). Nickname sizes also differ between the sides, and the vertical rhythm differs, with a big empty gap under the shrunken name.
Lock only changes the WINNER tag from yellow to white. This is a weak cue that viewers may not notice (G-56, G-57).
answer.reasons: With the brief's own values the card is clean, symmetric and readable. The Red wins, Blue wins and Clear steps all work, and no text collides or clips in any frame. The long-value frames show the problems. The gym logos sit on their own contrast discs, and the gym-and-record line is set larger than the boxer's name, which inverts the hierarchy. Shrinking one long name leaves the two corners visibly unequal in type size and spacing. A director would send it back for those fixes instead of airing it as delivered.

otherProblems: The panel stays the same width, so with the sample values about the right 40% of the card is empty (G-2 to G-4). The text never ends up stranded in a corner, though.

A short, faint orange hairline sits in the bottom-right corner (around x 1680–1795). It doesn't change length during hold, so it doesn't read as a timer. It's barely visible, but it looks a little stray.
With empty values (G-8 to G-10) the full-size card shows only 'DONATION' top left and is otherwise blank. A real alert would always have a name, so this is only an edge case.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, readable alert card at the top right. A dark plate, an orange edge bar and a ringed avatar sit beside a clear stack of label and amount, a bold name and a lighter message. It reads well on the dark, light and busy grounds. The long name with umlauts and Å fits in full, the long message wraps to two lines and the card grows to hold it, and the white shield avatar shows clearly inside its dark ring. The take, out, update, hold, resume, replay and skip frames all behave as expected. Hold keeps the alert up at 10 s, resume and skip clear it, and replay plays the entrance again. The only issues are design nits: empty space on the right of the fixed-width card with short values, and a faint stray hairline. Neither is enough to keep it off air.

otherProblems: Gym logos sit on circular plates of their own: a black disc behind the white crest and a white disc behind the dark one (G-4/G-5, crops G-65/G-66). The plates don't belong to the type around them.

Gym logos are missing with the sample values (G-2/G-3) and with both one-sided long values (G-8 to G-11), even when the gym name is shown. Logos only appear when every field is long, so whether the card shows logos looks random.

The gym name is pushed into the record line in large mixed-case type ('Kaunas BC · 14-3', 'St. Michael's ABC · 11-2'). It sits under a 'RECORD' label and is bigger than the boxer's name above it, so the hierarchy reads backwards.

The two corners get unequal type under stress. In G-8/G-9 the red name drops to a small single line while the blue name stays large. In G-4 the red name and nickname are noticeably smaller than the blue ones, and the blue name wraps to two lines, so the face-off looks lopsided.
The locked state is shown only by the WINNER badge turning from yellow to white (G-56). A viewer or operator would hardly notice the change.
answer.reasons: The sample layout is clean: the red/blue split, the weight-class header, the VS plate, and readable diacritics with no clipping. Picking a winner, locking it and clearing it all work, and the losing side dims without losing legibility. It fails on the desk checks. The gym logos sit on separate circular plates, and they appear only when every field is long. The gym name is crammed into the record line at a larger size than the boxer's name. Long names make the two corners visibly unequal in type size, which a face-off card can't afford.

otherProblems: The panel is a fixed width, so with short sample values about the right 40% of it sits empty (G-2 to G-4). It reads as left-aligned rather than broken, but a tighter or auto-sized width would balance better.
The countdown line at the bottom right of the panel is so thin and faint it barely shows (G-2, G-5). Viewers will hardly notice it, so it doesn't do much.
With empty values (G-8 to G-10), only the 'DONATION' label sits in an otherwise empty panel. This is a degenerate case an operator wouldn't put to air.
Next (G-41 to G-45) changes nothing. The brief doesn't ask for that action.
answer.reasons: G would air. It's a clean dark alert card at the top right: an orange accent bar, a ringed avatar, a monospaced label and amount, a bold name and a grey message. All text reads well on the video, light and busy grounds. The long umlaut username fits on one line, the long message wraps cleanly to two lines inside the panel, and the white shield avatar sits well inside its orange ring. Nothing is clipped or overlapping. Skip, replay, hold and resume all work as the brief needs: skip clears the card fast, replay re-animates it, hold keeps it up past 10 s, and resume lets it time out. The only weak points are the empty right side with short values and a near-invisible timer line, and neither is a reason to keep it off air.

otherProblems: In the stress frames the two long director names break at their hyphens onto two lines ('Okonkwo-/Fitzgerald', 'Vasconcelos-/Albuquerque'). Those top cards get three lines while the bottom cards get two, so the rows look slightly uneven.
The reveal marks the winner only with a gold-tinted card and glow. There is no 'WINNER' label, so the moment depends on colour alone.
After suspense and reveal, the non-winning nominees are dimmed quite far. This is deliberate, but on a busy LED-wall feed they will fade back a lot.
answer.reasons: This would air as delivered. It's a clean, centred black-and-gold card that sits well over the video, light and busy backgrounds because its near-opaque dark panel keeps every line readable. The long category title fits inside the frame, and the long names wrap neatly inside their cards with nothing cut off or spilling out. The suspense step dims the nominees and the reveal lights up the winner in gold; both steps work and nothing collides at any point in the take, update or out. The only issues are small: a little unevenness when the long names wrap, and a winner state with no 'WINNER' label.

otherProblems: Suspense (G-21/G-22) only dims the four cards and scales the board up slightly, so the change is quiet rather than dramatic.
In the stress frames (G-5 to G-7), long hyphenated names wrap at the hyphen onto two lines. This sits the text a little higher in those two cards than in the one-line cards.
After the reveal (G-27), the three losing cards are dimmed to low-contrast grey. This is on purpose, but they are hard to read.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board with a double gold frame. The type hierarchy is clear: a gold kicker, a bold white category, a short gold rule, then four equal cards with the title over a director line. It stays readable over the video, light and busy grounds because its panel is solid. The long category fits on one line inside the frame, as the native crop shows. Long names wrap neatly inside their cards, and nothing is clipped or overlapping. Suspense and reveal are both on the operator surface. Reveal gives the winner a gold-filled, glowing card and dims the others, which is clear and cinematic. The take, update and out transitions are clean, and with empty values the board degrades sensibly to just the category. It would air as delivered.

otherProblems: Each team logo sits on its own bordered square plate (G-2, G-4, G-5). The right one is a bright white/light-grey tile on the dark glass bar, and it reads as a separate box rather than as part of the design.
Next map (G-47 to G-52) changes nothing on screen. The bar still reads KARTTA 1, so no frame shows the map advancing.
Pressing Resume after the technical pause (G-81 to G-86) returns the bar to ENNEN OTTELUA, not to a live state, so the phase can read pre-match during play.
With long names, Team A's name is set noticeably smaller than Team B's (G-5, G-11, G-87), so the two sides are typeset unequally.
In the empty-values state (G-8 to G-10) the right half of the bar is a large void beside the score box, so the bar looks lopsided.
answer.reasons: I'd hold this one, though there are no basic mistakes. It's a clean, well-built dark glass scorebug: team names, map, BO5 pips and the Finnish phase pill are readable on the light, video and busy grounds, and the long names wrap inside their fields without clipping. Go live (LIVE), Pause (TAUKO) and Map final after Go live (LOPPU) all show on screen. What keeps it off air is mainly the logos: each crest sits on its own bordered square plate, and the bright white plate behind the burgundy crest stands out as a separate box on the dark bar. Next map was only tested before going live, and nothing changes in those frames. Resume after a pause goes back to the pre-match word, not live. Long names get uneven type sizes on the two sides. It's close, but it needs the logo treatment fixed before it airs.

otherProblems: Each team logo sits on its own bordered square plate, and the two plates don't match: the pale-yellow hexagon is on a dark tile, while the burgundy crest is on a bright white/pink tile that stands out as a light square on the dark glass bar (G-2, G-4, G-90, G-91).
Next map was pressed from pre-match (G-47–G-52) and nothing visibly changed: the board still says KARTTA 1 and the pips are the same. No frame shows the board moving to the next map.
The live phase word is the English 'LIVE' (G-25–G-28), but the brief asks for Finnish phase words. The other three are Finnish: ENNEN OTTELUA, TAUKO, LOPPU.

With long names the two sides use different type sizes: TAMPEREEN TEKNILLINEN YLIOPISTO ESPORTS on the left is set noticeably smaller and sits higher than ÅBO AKADEMI GAMING SOCIETY on the right (G-5, G-11).
In the empty-values frames (G-8–G-10) Team A's name stays while the whole right side is blank, which leaves the bar lopsided.
answer.reasons: There are no basic mistakes. No text overlaps or gets clipped, the long names wrap cleanly in every stress frame, contrast holds on the light and busy grounds, and Take, Out, Live, Pause, Resume, Final and the per-side map score all work. The deciding problem is the logos: each sits on its own square plate, one dark and one bright white, and the white plate shows up as a light square on the dark bar. The brief's pale-yellow and dark-burgundy logos needed to sit on the glass directly. Smaller points: Next map showed no visible effect, the live state says 'LIVE' instead of a Finnish word, and long names get unequal type sizes on the two sides. It's close, but it would need a few fixes before air.
